# Report Card

> Building a unit of anything emits its report card. The card is not documentation
> bolted on after — it is the durable artifact the work is born with, the SEED the
> work spawns from, and the honest, graded, two-way-linked account of what the unit
> does and which of its innards do it. A unit shipped without its card is incomplete.

Domain-agnostic. The skin changes (Gherkin for code, circuit-block Given/When/Then
for electronics, request/response for an API); the skeleton never does.

**This skill ships working machinery, not just doctrine.** If a repo has no card
system, install it — don't hand-write prose that evaporates with the conversation.

---

## DO THIS FIRST — is the machinery present?

```bash
ls features/*.feature 2>/dev/null | head -3   # cards exist?
git config core.hooksPath                     # should print .githooks
```

**No cards / no hooks → install, then card.** One command, idempotent, never commits:

```bash
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh            # current repo, features/
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/install.sh --target /path/to/repo \
    --cards-dir features --title "Foo — Feature Reference"
```

It drops into the repo:

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `features/print-card.py` | cards → `README.md` + printable `dist/` |
| `features/gen-status.py` | cards → `STATUS.md` (the derived test matrix) |
| `features/gen-sessions.py` | Codex transcripts → `SESSIONS.generated.md` |
| `features/cards.conf` | per-repo knobs (title, source extensions, exclusions) |
| `features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt` | the house-style skeleton to copy |
| `features/INDEX.md` | the commit ⇄ card map (the one hand-kept file) |
| `.githooks/pre-commit` + `post-merge` + `report-card-stamp.sh` | the stamp engine |
| `.githooks/pre-commit.local` | repo-local jobs — **yours, never clobbered on reinstall** |
| `core.hooksPath = .githooks` | set for this clone (git won't auto-run committed hooks) |

Then, **every commit onward, with zero effort:** a diff touching a card's `# WATCH:`
symbols stamps a dated RESULT-LOG line into that card *in the same commit*, and a
staged card regenerates `STATUS.md` / `README.md` / `SESSIONS.generated.md` and stages
them too. Mapping is **by symbol, not filename** — touching an unrelated part of a
shared file does not tag every card.

Already installed elsewhere and want the engine refreshed? Re-run `install.sh`; it
overwrites the canonical hooks + generators and keeps `pre-commit.local`, `cards.conf`,
`INDEX.md`, and every card. `--force` to overwrite those too.

## Then: write the card (the same motion as the build)

1. `cp features/TEMPLATE.feature.txt features/<name>.feature` and fill it in.
2. Write `features/<name>.session.md` — the spawning conversation, faithful not
   flattering, with the mandatory **How to get back** block.
3. Back-link the innards: `// REPORT-CARD >> features/<name>.feature` (comment syntax
   of that language).
4. Set the card's `# WATCH:` line to the symbols it owns — that's the hook contract.
5. Enrol it in `features/INDEX.md`.
6. `python3 features/print-card.py --readme` (and `--all` for printable `dist/`).
7. Commit. The hooks do the rest.

**House style, grade ladder, banned anti-patterns:** `reference/house-style.md`.
**Why the format is shaped this way:** `reference/wiki-pattern.md`.

## Just report back to me (works WITHOUT git)

```bash
~/.Codex/skills/report-card/scripts/report.sh --target ~/work/foo
```

Regenerates every derived view and prints an honest summary: card count, scenario
count, grades in use, and the three failure modes that otherwise stay silent —
cards with **no `# WATCH:` line** (the hooks can never stamp them), cards whose
grade is written as a **trailing comment** instead of a Gherkin tag (no generator
counts it, so they show as ungraded), and cards with **no `.session.md`** (broken
triad). Finds the card home automatically (`features/`, `cards/`, `docs/cards`).

**Git is optional.** Cards, generators and all derived views work on a plain
folder — `install.sh` detects a non-git target, installs everything except the
hooks, and says so. Only RESULT-LOG *stamping* needs git, because it has to know
which symbols a diff touched. In a non-git folder you run `report.sh` yourself
instead of a commit doing it for you.

## cards.conf keys

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `title` | heading of the generated reference |
| `readme_file` | target for `--readme` (default `README.md`) — **set this if `features/README.md` is hand-written**, or it gets clobbered |
| `source_ext` | extensions recognised as "innards" in a `# cite:` line |
| `meta_prefix` | card-name prefixes grouped as meta/process cards |
| `exclude` | cards kept out of `STATUS.md` (rollups, host-side tooling) |
| `readme_exclude` | cards hidden from the reference entirely (rare) |
| `grade_map` | translate a repo's OWN grade words into canonical tiers, e.g. `@untested-in-renoise:@runtime-untested, @built:@code-verified` — the project keeps its vocabulary AND gets a correct matrix |
| `runtime_label` / `hardware_label` / `status_note` | STATUS.md column labels + note |
| `sessions_file` | session-registry filename (default `SESSIONS.generated.md`) |
| `project_dirs` | extra paths whose Codex transcripts belong to this repo |

## Card dialects — indented banners are legal

Some repos put the banner **inside** the `Feature:` block, indented (Paketti does).
The stamp engine matches `# WATCH:` / `RESULT-LOG >>` at **line start with leading
whitespace allowed**, so both dialects stamp, and the inserted line copies the
marker's own indentation. What is still rejected is a *mid-sentence* mention of the
marker in prose, so a card describing the convention can't opt itself in.

A strict column-0 anchor is what made every Paketti card a silent no-op for months —
hooks installed, running, stamping nothing, no error. If cards aren't being stamped,
run `report.sh` before assuming the hooks are broken.

## Verification commands

```bash
python3 features/print-card.py --readme     # regenerate the feature reference
python3 features/print-card.py --all        # per-card dist/ (pure Gherkin + printable)
python3 features/gen-status.py              # regenerate the test matrix
python3 features/gen-sessions.py            # regenerate the session registry
rtfc features/dist/<name>.card.md           # printable card → RTF clipboard
```

All are dependency-free Apple-native python3, deterministic (no timestamps embedded,
so no commit churn), and resolve the card home from `--cards-dir` → `$REPORT_CARDS_DIR`
→ the script's own directory.

---

## The four properties (every card, every domain)

1. **Verifiable claims** — condition → action → expected result.
   `Given <state>, When <action>, Then <measurable outcome>`.
2. **Linked to the innards** — each claim cites the exact parts that satisfy it
   (proc + line + commit; component refdes + node; file + function).
3. **Honestly graded** — one tag per claim. The grade is the anti-lying mechanism.
   `@designed` `@built` `@build-verified` `@sim-verified` `@runtime-verified`
   `@hw-verified` `@untested` `@hw-untested` `@todo` `@stock`.
   Untested is untested. **Never grade up to look finished.**
4. **Two-way** — the innards carry a greppable back-link to the card, so the wiki is
   bidirectional.

## The triad — three legs, all cross-linked

- **`<name>.feature` (the card)** — the spec: graded verifiable claims, each cited to
  its innards. The *what* + *why-as-grade*.
- **`<name>.session.md`** — the spawning conversation stored beside the card: the
  requests, refinements, corrections, rejected options, the "no I didn't do it"
  admissions. **Faithful, not flattering** — the grade's audit trail. This enables the
  **vibe diff**: across versions you diff the code, the card, AND the dialogue that
  drove each change. A card without its session can spawn the code but not the vibe —
  INCOMPLETE.
  **MANDATORY "How to get back" block** — transcript `file://` path, session ID,
  `Codex --resume <id>`, real date+timestamps pulled from the transcript (never
  fabricated; if unconfirmable, say so). `gen-sessions.py` discovers these repo-wide.
  **MANDATORY bundle, don't just link** — a `file://` link rots the moment the
  `.jsonl` moves. Copy the raw transcript beside the card as
  `<name>.transcript.jsonl` (lossless) plus a readable `<name>.transcript.md`. The
  curated `.session.md` is the audit; the bundled transcript is the source.
- **RESULT block** (card header) — what actually shipped: feature commit(s), the PR if
  any ("direct-push, no PR" when none), card-authoring commit(s), files changed.
  Verify delivery by first-parent ancestry — don't guess; watch duplicate PR numbers
  across forks. The hooks maintain the running RESULT-LOG under it.

Three legs cross-linked ⇒ the wiki is rebuildable straight from git: load one card →
spec + rationale + diff, no re-reading raw source.

## The card is a generative seed (it comes first)

The card opens with a **WHAT THIS CARD SPAWNS** preamble because it spawns three spaces:

- **Codespace** = the file structure — the card's own files plus the innards layout it
  cites. From the card you can scaffold or re-derive the code.
- **Thinkspace** = the reasoning — held in the `.session` (wrong turns included). Also
  what the vibe diff diffs.
- **Areaspace** = the domain boundary — what the unit owns and must NOT touch, so
  re-spawning stays in-bounds. Make it verifiable with a `@stock` "must not break"
  scenario.

`card ⇒ codespace + areaspace`; `session ⇒ thinkspace`.

## Tests → Features → automatic index (never hand-typed)

The whole point is that **code conveys its own verified status** — a behaviour is
written ONCE and every status view derives from it:

1. **Tests ARE the Features.** A verifiable claim lives once as a graded `Scenario`;
   its `@grade` tags **are** its test status.
2. **Features become the index.** The status view is GENERATED from those tags, run
   automatically by the pre-commit hook, committed alongside the card.
3. **So anyone can confirm** with zero manual labour: tested or not, at what level, and
   where it links (card → innards → commits → session).

**Banned anti-pattern:** hand-maintaining a parallel "what's tested" list. If you catch
yourself typing `runtime-verified` into an index, stop — change the card's tag and let
the index regenerate. A derived view cannot disagree with its source; a hand-kept one
drifts and lies. Generated files carry a `DO NOT EDIT — generated` header.

## Relationship to Convey (`~/work/convey`)

**This skill is the DOCTRINE + SKIN SYSTEM + portable tooling. Convey is the larger
ENGINE.** A report card IS a Convey "Underlying Principle" — a `principles/NNNN-slug/`
folder bound to git. The hooks shipped…9612 tokens truncated…n must offer ascending/descending ping-pong cycles.
- The Pattern drag-bar editor should have its own persisted hide flag, independent from Hide Details, so users can keep the controls visible while hiding only the contour editor.
- Music Mouse should treat a selected non-Music-Mouse sample as protected: sound keys warn instead of regenerating or retriggering it, and active contour playback should adopt mouse-position changes on the clock instead of adding immediate off-grid strikes.
- Music Mouse transpose shortcuts must update both the audible notes and the visual readout/canvas; on ISO/Finnish layouts Shift-< should be treated as the upward transpose gesture even if Renoise reports the key name as `<`.
- Music Mouse transpose shortcuts should update the grid state silently when Music Mouse is frozen, keyjazzing, sound-disabled, or mouse-muted; they must not re-trigger the cursor chord from a muted mode.
- Music Mouse Plink should keep its fast percussive decay character but use a longer generated strike, so it reads as a short pitched system sound instead of a pitchless thud.
- Music Mouse Record-to-Pattern stays on right Shift; standalone left Shift must not trigger playback and must leave Shift combos like Shift-< usable. The standalone trigger-this-grid-entry gesture moves from left Shift to standalone Option/Alt.
- Music Mouse `interval` means transpose step size for z/x/<, not a live pattern-playback interval; the UI should name it accordingly.
- Music Mouse Strike controls are sound-design/render controls, not performance gestures: Plink/Bell/Gong, Length, Decay, and Bell/Sustain should render/update the instrument silently; i/o/p and standalone Option/Alt trigger the selected grid entry.

## decisions

- Velocity layers are GROUPS, not splits. Each group carries its own key range
  and its own velocity range (>Min/>Max); splits only subdivide a group by key.
  So Joshua's question "does the Voice format support velocity zones at the
  format level" is answered yes, and the implementation is N groups with
  overlapping key ranges and stacked velocity ranges.
- Trim exported waves at the loop end. The TX16W has no loop end, so not
  trimming makes the sampler play a longer loop than Renoise does. Lossless.
- Budget RAM against uncompressed frames, not file size. DWVW shrinks the disk
  copy only; the sampler holds the decoded audio.
- The 8-byte trailer on every Wave/Voic/Perf reference is a disk name. Writing
  the real volume label is what makes the sampler prompt for a named floppy.

  third-party code, unloaded dev scripts) go in `_DUP_ALLOWED` in .spine/check.py with a

# report-card knobs for Paketti. Read by print-card.py / gen-status.py / gen-sessions.py.

title       = Paketti — Feature Reference

# IMPORTANT: features/README.md here is HAND-WRITTEN (it explains the DreamGraph
# intent layer). The generated reference goes to CARDS.md so README.md is never

readme_file = CARDS.md

# Paketti is Lua + a little Python/XML; these are the extensions recognised as
# "innards" when a scenario's # cite: line names a file.
source_ext  = .lua,.py,.xml,.md

# Dated conversation rollups are meta cards, not product behaviours.
meta_prefix = session-,day-,2026-

# Kept out of the STATUS matrix: the skeleton and the doc example are not
# Paketti behaviours.

# Renoise is the runtime; there is no separate "hardware" tier for most cards,
# but MIDI-controller cards (LPD8, grid controllers) genuinely are hardware.
# Paketti keeps its OWN grade words (they mean something here); this teaches the
# status matrix which canonical tier each one is, without renaming anything.
#   @built              = the module ships and loads — Lua has no compile step,
#                         so the honest equivalent of the "build" tier is code-level.
#   @untested-in-renoise= written but never exercised live -> runtime-untested
#   @in-renoise / @mcp-verified / @user-verified = actually exercised live
#   @logic-verified     = reasoned through / traced, not run -> code tier
grade_map = @built:@code-verified, @logic-verified:@code-verified, @untested-in-renoise:@runtime-untested, @in-renoise:@runtime-verified, @mcp-verified:@runtime-verified, @user-verified:@runtime-verified

hardware_label = MIDI hardware
status_note    = Runtime = exercised live in Renoise. MIDI hardware = confirmed on the actual controller.

# report-card knobs for Paketti. Read by print-card.py / gen-status.py / gen-sessions.py.

title       = Paketti — Feature Reference

# IMPORTANT: features/README.md here is HAND-WRITTEN (it explains the DreamGraph
# intent layer). The generated reference goes to CARDS.md so README.md is never
# clobbered by --readme.
readme_file = CARDS.md

# Paketti is Lua + a little Python/XML; these are the extensions recognised as
# "innards" when a scenario's # cite: line names a file.
source_ext  = .lua,.py,.xml,.md

# Dated conversation rollups are meta cards, not product behaviours.
meta_prefix = session-,day-,2026-

# Kept out of the STATUS matrix: the skeleton and the doc example are not
# Paketti behaviours.
exclude     = TEMPLATE.feature,pattern-editor-example.feature

# Renoise is the runtime; there is no separate "hardware" tier for most cards,
# but MIDI-controller cards (LPD8, grid controllers) genuinely are hardware.
# Paketti keeps its OWN grade words (they mean something here); this teaches the
# status matrix which canonical tier each one is, without renaming anything.
#   @built              = the module ships and loads — Lua has no compile step,
#                         so the honest equivalent of the "build" tier is code-level.
#   @untested-in-renoise= written but never exercised live -> runtime-untested
#   @in-renoise / @mcp-verified / @user-verified = actually exercised live
#   @logic-verified     = reasoned through / traced, not run -> code tier
grade_map = @built:@code-verified, @logic-verified:@code-verified, @untested-in-renoise:@runtime-untested, @in-renoise:@runtime-verified, @mcp-verified:@runtime-verified, @user-verified:@runtime-verified

runtime_label  = Runtime (Renoise)
hardware_label = MIDI hardware
status_note    = Runtime = exercised live in Renoise. MIDI hardware = confirmed on the actual controller.

+-- FEATURE-CARD >> features/note-off-cleanup.feature
+-- Inspired by Phaos's SimpleNotesOff: clear the OFF note only, preserving
+-- every neighboring field, and include hidden note columns.
+local function PakettiClearPatternTrackNoteOffs(pattern, track_index)
+  local pattern_track = pattern.tracks[track_index]
+  if pattern_track.is_empty then return 0 end
+  local count = 0
+  for line_index = 1, pattern.number_of_lines do
+    local line = pattern_track:line(line_index)
+    if not line.is_empty then
+      for _, note in ipairs(line.note_columns) do
+        if note.note_value == 120 then
+          note.note_value = 121
+          count = count + 1
+        end
+      end
+    end
+  end
+  return count
+end
+
+local function PakettiDeleteNoteOffs(all_tracks, whole_song, label)
+  local song = renoise.song()
+  if not song then return end
+  local track_indices = {}
+  if all_tracks then
+    for index, track in ipairs(song.tracks) do
+      if track.type == renoise.Track.TRACK_TYPE_SEQUENCER then
+        track_indices[#track_indices + 1] = index
+      end
+    end
+  else
+    if song.selected_track.type ~= renoise.Track.TRACK_TYPE_SEQUENCER then
+      renoise.app():show_status("Paketti: Select a sequencer track to delete note offs")
+      return
+    end
+    track_indices[1] = song.selected_track_index
+  end
+
+  song:describe_undo("Delete Note Offs in " .. label)
+  local patterns = whole_song and song.patterns or {song.selected_pattern}
+  local count = 0
+  for _, pattern in ipairs(patterns) do
+    for _, track_index in ipairs(track_indices) do
+      count = count + PakettiClearPatternTrackNoteOffs(pattern, track_index)
+    end
+  end
+  renoise.app():show_status(string.format("Paketti: Deleted %d note off%s in %s",
+    count, count == 1 and "" or "s", label))

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Simple Interpolation
--
-- Set the interpolation (and Anti-aliasing) of samples from the Tools menu,
-- the sample list, sample editor and instrument box menus, or your own keys
-- (Preferences > Keys > Global > Simple Interpolation):
--
--   Selected Sample      the sample selected in Renoise
--   Selected Instrument  every sample of the selected instrument
--   Whole Song           every sample of every instrument
--   New Samples          a default for every sample you load, record or
--                        drag in from now on, in place of Renoise's own
--
-- by phaos & claude
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local TOOL = "Simple Interpolation"
local MODES = { "None", "Linear", "Cubic", "Sinc" }   -- = INTERPOLATE_*

local prefs = renoise.Document.create("SimpleInterpolationPreferences") {
  new_mode = 0,          -- New Samples: 0 Renoise's default, else 1 - 4
  new_aa = false,        -- New Samples: Anti-aliasing on
}
renoise.tool().preferences = prefs

local function status(msg)
  renoise.app():show_status(TOOL .. ": " .. msg)
end

local function song()
  local ok, s = pcall(renoise.song)
  return ok and s or nil
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Selected Sample / Selected Instrument / Whole Song
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local SCOPES = { "Selected Sample", "Selected Instrument", "Whole Song" }

-- the samples a scope means, and how to say so
local function targets(scope)
  local s, list = song(), {}
  if not s then return list, "" end
  if scope == "Selected Sample" then
    local smp = s.selected_sample
    if smp then list[1] = smp end
    return list, "Selected sample"
  end
  local insts = scope == "Selected Instrument" and { s.selected_instrument }
                or s.instruments
  for _, inst in ipairs(insts) do
    for _, smp in ipairs(inst.samples) do list[#list + 1] = smp end
  end
  local what = scope == "Selected Instrument" and "Selected instrument"
               or "Whole song"
  return list, string.format("%s (%d sample%s)", what, #list,
                             #list == 1 and "" or "s")
end

-- the interpolation all of them share (nil: none, or mixed)
local function common(scope)
  local list, m = targets(scope), nil
  for _, smp in ipairs(list) do
    if m and smp.interpolation_mode ~= m then return nil end
    m = smp.interpolation_mode
  end
  return m
end

local function all_aa(scope)
  local list = targets(scope)
  if #list == 0 then return false end
  for _, smp in ipairs(list) do
    if not smp.oversample_enabled then return false end
  end
  return true
end

-- change every sample of a scope: one undo step
local function change(scope, what_of, fn)
  local list, what = targets(scope)
  if #list == 0 then
    status(scope == "Selected Sample" and "No sample selected"
           or "No samples")
    return
  end
  pcall(function() song():describe_undo(TOOL .. ": " .. what_of) end)
  for _, smp in ipairs(list) do pcall(fn, smp) end
  status(what .. ": " .. what_of)
end

local function set_mode(scope, mode)
  change(scope, MODES[mode], function(smp) smp.interpolation_mode = mode end)
end

local function cycle(scope)
  local list = targets(scope)
  local m = common(scope) or (list[1] and list[1].interpolation_mode) or 3
  set_mode(scope, m % #MODES + 1)
end

local function toggle_aa(scope)
  local on = not all_aa(scope)
  change(scope, "Anti-aliasing " .. (on and "on" or "off"),
         function(smp) smp.oversample_enabled = on end)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- New Samples
--
-- A sample is new when audio arrives in an empty slot, or a file is loaded
-- over one (its audio and its name change together). It gets the default
-- only where it still has Renoise's own setting, so a sample that comes
-- with its own (a duplicate, an instrument file, another tool's choice) is
-- left alone. Renoise's own setting is read from the empty slots it makes.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local W = { song = nil, insts = {}, fresh = {} }
local RENOISE = { mode = 3, aa = false }       -- what an empty slot has

local function apply_new(smp)
  local m, aa = prefs.new_mode.value, prefs.new_aa.value
  if m > 0 and smp.interpolation_mode == RENOISE.mode and m ~= RENOISE.mode then
    smp.interpolation_mode = m
  end
  if aa and smp.oversample_enabled == RENOISE.aa and not RENOISE.aa then
    smp.oversample_enabled = true
  end
end

local function learn(smp)                       -- an empty slot: Renoise's own
  if smp and not smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data then
    RENOISE.mode = smp.interpolation_mode
    RENOISE.aa = smp.oversample_enabled
  end
end

local function unwatch(list)
  for _, w in ipairs(list) do
    pcall(function() w[1]:remove_notifier(w[2]) end)
  end
end

local function watch_sample(list, smp)
  local st = { data = smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data, name = smp.name }
  local function on_buffer()
    local data = smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data
    if data and (not st.data or smp.name ~= st.name) then
      pcall(apply_new, smp)
      st.fresh = false
    elseif data then                 -- new audio, same name so far: a file
      st.fresh = true                -- loaded over it gets its name next
      W.fresh[#W.fresh + 1] = st
    end
    st.data, st.name = data, smp.name
  end
  local function on_name()
    if st.fresh then st.fresh = false pcall(apply_new, smp) end
    st.name = smp.name
  end
  smp.sample_buffer_observable:add_notifier(on_buffer)
  smp.name_observable:add_notifier(on_name)
  list[#list + 1] = { smp.sample_buffer_observable, on_buffer }
  list[#list + 1] = { smp.name_observable, on_name }
end

local function watch_instrument(inst)
  local w = { samples = {} }
  local function samples()
    unwatch(w.samples)
    w.samples = {}
    for _, smp in ipairs(inst.samples) do watch_sample(w.samples, smp) end
  end
  w.fn = function(ev)
    if ev.type == "insert" then learn(inst.samples[ev.index]) end
    samples()
  end
  inst.samples_observable:add_notifier(w.fn)
  w.obs = inst.samples_observable
  samples()
  return w
end

local function unwatch_all()
  for _, w in ipairs(W.insts) do
    unwatch(w.samples)
    pcall(function() w.obs:remove_notifier(w.fn) end)
  end
  W.insts = {}
end

local function watch_all()
  unwatch_all()
  local s = song()
  if not s then return end
  for _, inst in ipairs(s.instruments) do
    local ok, w = pcall(watch_instrument, inst)
    if ok then W.insts[#W.insts + 1] = w end
  end
end

local function on_instruments(ev)
  if ev.type == "insert" then
    local inst = song().instruments[ev.index]
    if inst then learn(inst.samples[1]) end
  end
  watch_all()
end

local function attach()
  local s = song()
  if not s then return end
  if W.song then
    pcall(function() W.song.instruments_observable:remove_notifier(on_instruments) end)
  end
  W.song = s
  s.instruments_observable:add_notifier(on_instruments)
  watch_all()
end

renoise.tool().app_new_document_observable:add_notifier(attach)
renoise.tool().app_release_document_observable:add_notifier(function()
  unwatch_all()
  if W.song then
    pcall(function() W.song.instruments_observable:remove_notifier(on_instruments) end)
  end
  W.song = nil
end)
-- a file loaded over a sample: its name follows within the same moment
renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:add_notifier(function()
  if #W.fresh > 0 then
    for _, st in ipairs(W.fresh) do st.fresh = false end
    W.fresh = {}
  end
end)
attach()

local function set_new(m)
  prefs.new_mode.value = m
  status("New samples: " .. (m == 0 and "Off (Renoise's default)" or MODES[m]))
end

local function toggle_new_aa()
  prefs.new_aa.value = not prefs.new_aa.value
  status("New samples: Anti-aliasing " .. (prefs.new_aa.value and "on"
         or "as Renoise sets it"))
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Menus and key bindings
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function entry(name, invoke, selected)
  renoise.tool():add_menu_entry { name = name, invoke = invoke,
                                  selected = selected }
end

-- one scope's entries under `base`: the four modes, then Anti-aliasing
local function scope_menu(base, scope)
  for i, m in ipairs(MODES) do
    entry(base .. scope .. ":" .. m,
          function() set_mode(scope, i) end,
          function() return common(scope) == i end)
  end
  entry("--- " .. base .. scope .. ":Anti-aliasing",
        function() toggle_aa(scope) end,
        function() return all_aa(scope) end)
end

-- Tools menu: everything
local TOOLS = "Main Menu:Tools:" .. TOOL .. ":"
entry(TOOLS .. "New Samples:Off (Renoise's Default)", function() set_new(0) end,
      function() return prefs.new_mode.value == 0 end)
for i, m in ipairs(MODES) do
  entry((i == 1 and "--- " or "") .. TOOLS .. "New Samples:" .. m,
        function() set_new(i) end,
        function() return prefs.new_mode.value == i end)
end
entry("--- " .. TOOLS .. "New Samples:Anti-aliasing On", toggle_new_aa,
      function() return prefs.new_aa.value end)
for _, scope in ipairs(SCOPES) do scope_menu(TOOLS, scope) end

-- right-click menus where the samples are
for _, place in ipairs { "Sample List", "Sample Editor" } do
  local base = place .. ":" .. TOOL .. ":"
  scope_menu(base, "Selected Sample")
  scope_menu(base, "Selected Instrument")
end
do
  local base = "Instrument Box:" .. TOOL .. ":"
  scope_menu(base, "Selected Instrument")
  scope_menu(base, "Whole Song")
end

-- key bindings
local function bind(name, fn)
  renoise.tool():add_keybinding {
    name = "Global:" .. TOOL .. ":" .. name,
    invoke = function(repeated) if not repeated then fn() end end,
  }
end
for _, scope in ipairs(SCOPES) do
  for i, m in ipairs(MODES) do
    bind(scope .. " - " .. m, function() set_mode(scope, i) end)
  end
  bind(scope .. " - Cycle", function() cycle(scope) end)
  bind(scope .. " - Toggle Anti-aliasing", function() toggle_aa(scope) end)
end
bind("New Samples - Cycle", function()
  set_new((prefs.new_mode.value + 1) % (#MODES + 1))
end)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Simple Interpolation
--
-- Set the interpolation (and Anti-aliasing) of samples from the Tools menu,
-- the sample list, sample editor and instrument box menus, or your own keys
-- (Preferences > Keys > Global > Simple Interpolation):
--
--   Selected Sample      the sample selected in Renoise
--   Selected Instrument  every sample of the selected instrument
--   Whole Song           every sample of every instrument
--   New Samples          a default for every sample you load, record or
--                        drag in from now on, in place of Renoise's own
--
-- by phaos & claude
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local TOOL = "Simple Interpolation"
local MODES = { "None", "Linear", "Cubic", "Sinc" }   -- = INTERPOLATE_*

local prefs = renoise.Document.create("SimpleInterpolationPreferences") {
  new_mode = 0,          -- New Samples: 0 Renoise's default, else 1 - 4
  new_aa = false,        -- New Samples: Anti-aliasing on
}
renoise.tool().preferences = prefs

local function status(msg)
  renoise.app():show_status(TOOL .. ": " .. msg)
end

local function song()
  local ok, s = pcall(renoise.song)
  return ok and s or nil
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Selected Sample / Selected Instrument / Whole Song
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local SCOPES = { "Selected Sample", "Selected Instrument", "Whole Song" }

-- the samples a scope means, and how to say so
local function targets(scope)
  local s, list = song(), {}
  if not s then return list, "" end
  if scope == "Selected Sample" then
    local smp = s.selected_sample
    if smp then list[1] = smp end
    return list, "Selected sample"
  end
  local insts = scope == "Selected Instrument" and { s.selected_instrument }
                or s.instruments
  for _, inst in ipairs(insts) do
    for _, smp in ipairs(inst.samples) do list[#list + 1] = smp end
  end
  local what = scope == "Selected Instrument" and "Selected instrument"
               or "Whole song"
  return list, string.format("%s (%d sample%s)", what, #list,
                             #list == 1 and "" or "s")
end

-- the interpolation all of them share (nil: none, or mixed)
local function common(scope)
  local list, m = targets(scope), nil
  for _, smp in ipairs(list) do
    if m and smp.interpolation_mode ~= m then return nil end
    m = smp.interpolation_mode
  end
  return m
end

local function all_aa(scope)
  local list = targets(scope)
  if #list == 0 then return false end
  for _, smp in ipairs(list) do
    if not smp.oversample_enabled then return false end
  end
  return true
end

-- change every sample of a scope: one undo step
local function change(scope, what_of, fn)
  local list, what = targets(scope)
  if #list == 0 then
    status(scope == "Selected Sample" and "No sample selected"
           or "No samples")
    return
  end
  pcall(function() song():describe_undo(TOOL .. ": " .. what_of) end)
  for _, smp in ipairs(list) do pcall(fn, smp) end
  status(what .. ": " .. what_of)
end

local function set_mode(scope, mode)
  change(scope, MODES[mode], function(smp) smp.interpolation_mode = mode end)
end

local function cycle(scope)
  local list = targets(scope)
  local m = common(scope) or (list[1] and list[1].interpolation_mode) or 3
  set_mode(scope, m % #MODES + 1)
end

local function toggle_aa(scope)
  local on = not all_aa(scope)
  change(scope, "Anti-aliasing " .. (on and "on" or "off"),
         function(smp) smp.oversample_enabled = on end)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- New Samples
--
-- A sample is new when audio arrives in an empty slot, or a file is loaded
-- over one (its audio and its name change together). It gets the default
-- only where it still has Renoise's own setting, so a sample that comes
-- with its own (a duplicate, an instrument file, another tool's choice) is
-- left alone. Renoise's own setting is read from the empty slots it makes.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local W = { song = nil, insts = {}, fresh = {} }
local RENOISE = { mode = 3, aa = false }       -- what an empty slot has

local function apply_new(smp)
  local m, aa = prefs.new_mode.value, prefs.new_aa.value
  if m > 0 and smp.interpolation_mode == RENOISE.mode and m ~= RENOISE.mode then
    smp.interpolation_mode = m
  end
  if aa and smp.oversample_enabled == RENOISE.aa and not RENOISE.aa then
    smp.oversample_enabled = true
  end
end

local function learn(smp)                       -- an empty slot: Renoise's own
  if smp and not smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data then
    RENOISE.mode = smp.interpolation_mode
    RENOISE.aa = smp.oversample_enabled
  end
end

local function unwatch(list)
  for _, w in ipairs(list) do
    pcall(function() w[1]:remove_notifier(w[2]) end)
  end
end

local function watch_sample(list, smp)
  local st = { data = smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data, name = smp.name }
  local function on_buffer()
    local data = smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data
    if data and (not st.data or smp.name ~= st.name) then
      pcall(apply_new, smp)
      st.fresh = false
    elseif data then                 -- new audio, same name so far: a file
      st.fresh = true                -- loaded over it gets its name next
      W.fresh[#W.fresh + 1] = st
    end
    st.data, st.name = data, smp.name
  end
  local function on_name()
    if st.fresh then st.fresh = false pcall(apply_new, smp) end
    st.name = smp.name
  end
  smp.sample_buffer_observable:add_notifier(on_buffer)
  smp.name_observable:add_notifier(on_name)
  list[#list + 1] = { smp.sample_buffer_observable, on_buffer }
  list[#list + 1] = { smp.name_observable, on_name }
end

local function watch_instrument(inst)
  local w = { samples = {} }
  local function samples()
    unwatch(w.samples)
    w.samples = {}
    for _, smp in ipairs(inst.samples) do watch_sample(w.samples, smp) end
  end
  w.fn = function(ev)
    if ev.type == "insert" then learn(inst.samples[ev.index]) end
    samples()
  end
  inst.samples_observable:add_notifier(w.fn)
  w.obs = inst.samples_observable
  samples()
  return w
end

local function unwatch_all()
  for _, w in ipairs(W.insts) do
    unwatch(w.samples)
    pcall(function() w.obs:remove_notifier(w.fn) end)
  end
  W.insts = {}
end

local function watch_all()
  unwatch_all()
  local s = song()
  if not s then return end
  for _, inst in ipairs(s.instruments) do
    local ok, w = pcall(watch_instrument, inst)
    if ok then W.insts[#W.insts + 1] = w end
  end
end

local function on_instruments(ev)
  if ev.type == "insert" then
    local inst = song().instruments[ev.index]
    if inst then learn(inst.samples[1]) end
  end
  watch_all()
end

local function attach()
  local s = song()
  if not s then return end
  if W.song then
    pcall(function() W.song.instruments_observable:remove_notifier(on_instruments) end)
  end
  W.song = s
  s.instruments_observable:add_notifier(on_instruments)
  watch_all()
end

renoise.tool().app_new_document_observable:add_notifier(attach)
renoise.tool().app_release_document_observable:add_notifier(function()
  unwatch_all()
  if W.song then
    pcall(function() W.song.instruments_observable:remove_notifier(on_instruments) end)
  end
  W.song = nil
end)
-- a file loaded over a sample: its name follows within the same moment
renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:add_notifier(function()
  if #W.fresh > 0 then
    for _, st in ipairs(W.fresh) do st.fresh = false end
    W.fresh = {}
  end
end)
attach()

local function set_new(m)
  prefs.new_mode.value = m
  status("New samples: " .. (m == 0 and "Off (Renoise's default)" or MODES[m]))
end

local function toggle_new_aa()
  prefs.new_aa.value = not prefs.new_aa.value
  status("New samples: Anti-aliasing " .. (prefs.new_aa.value and "on"
         or "as Renoise sets it"))
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Menus and key bindings
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function entry(name, invoke, selected)
  renoise.tool():add_menu_entry { name = name, invoke = invoke,
                                  selected = selected }
end

-- one scope's entries under `base`: the four modes, then Anti-aliasing
local function scope_menu(base, scope)
  for i, m in ipairs(MODES) do
    entry(base .. scope .. ":" .. m,
          function() set_mode(scope, i) end,
          function() return common(scope) == i end)
  end
  entry("--- " .. base .. scope .. ":Anti-aliasing",
        function() toggle_aa(scope) end,
        function() return all_aa(scope) end)
end

-- Tools menu: everything
local TOOLS = "Main Menu:Tools:" .. TOOL .. ":"
entry(TOOLS .. "New Samples:Off (Renoise's Default)", function() set_new(0) end,
      function() return prefs.new_mode.value == 0 end)
for i, m in ipairs(MODES) do
  entry((i == 1 and "--- " or "") .. TOOLS .. "New Samples:" .. m,
        function() set_new(i) end,
        function() return prefs.new_mode.value == i end)
end
entry("--- " .. TOOLS .. "New Samples:Anti-aliasing On", toggle_new_aa,
      function() return prefs.new_aa.value end)
for _, scope in ipairs(SCOPES) do scope_menu(TOOLS, scope) end

-- right-click menus where the samples are
for _, place in ipairs { "Sample List", "Sample Editor" } do
  local base = place .. ":" .. TOOL .. ":"
  scope_menu(base, "Selected Sample")
  scope_menu(base, "Selected Instrument")
end
do
  local base = "Instrument Box:" .. TOOL .. ":"
  scope_menu(base, "Selected Instrument")
  scope_menu(base, "Whole Song")
end

-- key bindings
local function bind(name, fn)
  renoise.tool():add_keybinding {
    name = "Global:" .. TOOL .. ":" .. name,
    invoke = function(repeated) if not repeated then fn() end end,
  }
end
for _, scope in ipairs(SCOPES) do
  for i, m in ipairs(MODES) do
    bind(scope .. " - " .. m, function() set_mode(scope, i) end)
  end
  bind(scope .. " - Cycle", function() cycle(scope) end)
  bind(scope .. " - Toggle Anti-aliasing", function() toggle_aa(scope) end)
end
bind("New Samples - Cycle", function()
  set_new((prefs.new_mode.value + 1) % (#MODES + 1))
end)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Simple Interpolation
--
-- Set the interpolation (and Anti-aliasing) of samples from the Tools menu,
-- the sample list, sample editor and instrument box menus, or your own keys
-- (Preferences > Keys > Global > Simple Interpolation):
--
--   Selected Sample      the sample selected in Renoise
--   Selected Instrument  every sample of the selected instrument
--   Whole Song           every sample of every instrument
--   New Samples          a default for every sample you load, record or
--                        drag in from now on, in place of Renoise's own
--
-- by phaos & claude
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local TOOL = "Simple Interpolation"
local MODES = { "None", "Linear", "Cubic", "Sinc" }   -- = INTERPOLATE_*

local prefs = renoise.Document.create("SimpleInterpolationPreferences") {
  new_mode = 0,          -- New Samples: 0 Renoise's default, else 1 - 4
  new_aa = false,        -- New Samples: Anti-aliasing on
}
renoise.tool().preferences = prefs

local function status(msg)
  renoise.app():show_status(TOOL .. ": " .. msg)
end

local function song()
  local ok, s = pcall(renoise.song)
  return ok and s or nil
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Selected Sample / Selected Instrument / Whole Song
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local SCOPES = { "Selected Sample", "Selected Instrument", "Whole Song" }

-- the samples a scope means, and how to say so
local function targets(scope)
  local s, list = song(), {}
  if not s then return list, "" end
  if scope == "Selected Sample" then
    local smp = s.selected_sample
    if smp then list[1] = smp end
    return list, "Selected sample"
  end
  local insts = scope == "Selected Instrument" and { s.selected_instrument }
                or s.instruments
  for _, inst in ipairs(insts) do
    for _, smp in ipairs(inst.samples) do list[#list + 1] = smp end
  end
  local what = scope == "Selected Instrument" and "Selected instrument"
               or "Whole song"
  return list, string.format("%s (%d sample%s)", what, #list,
                             #list == 1 and "" or "s")
end

-- the interpolation all of them share (nil: none, or mixed)
local function common(scope)
  local list, m = targets(scope), nil
  for _, smp in ipairs(list) do
    if m and smp.interpolation_mode ~= m then return nil end
    m = smp.interpolation_mode
  end
  return m
end

local function all_aa(scope)
  local list = targets(scope)
  if #list == 0 then return false end
  for _, smp in ipairs(list) do
    if not smp.oversample_enabled then return false end
  end
  return true
end

-- change every sample of a scope: one undo step
local function change(scope, what_of, fn)
  local list, what = targets(scope)
  if #list == 0 then
    status(scope == "Selected Sample" and "No sample selected"
           or "No samples")
    return
  end
  pcall(function() song():describe_undo(TOOL .. ": " .. what_of) end)
  for _, smp in ipairs(list) do pcall(fn, smp) end
  status(what .. ": " .. what_of)
end

local function set_mode(scope, mode)
  change(scope, MODES[mode], function(smp) smp.interpolation_mode = mode end)
end

local function cycle(scope)
  local list = targets(scope)
  local m = common(scope) or (list[1] and list[1].interpolation_mode) or 3
  set_mode(scope, m % #MODES + 1)
end

local function toggle_aa(scope)
  local on = not all_aa(scope)
  change(scope, "Anti-aliasing " .. (on and "on" or "off"),
         function(smp) smp.oversample_enabled = on end)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- New Samples
--
-- A sample is new when audio arrives in an empty slot, or a file is loaded
-- over one (its audio and its name change together). It gets the default
-- only where it still has Renoise's own setting, so a sample that comes
-- with its own (a duplicate, an instrument file, another tool's choice) is
-- left alone. Renoise's own setting is read from the empty slots it makes.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local W = { song = nil, insts = {}, fresh = {} }
local RENOISE = { mode = 3, aa = false }       -- what an empty slot has

local function apply_new(smp)
  local m, aa = prefs.new_mode.value, prefs.new_aa.value
  if m > 0 and smp.interpolation_mode == RENOISE.mode and m ~= RENOISE.mode then
    smp.interpolation_mode = m
  end
  if aa and smp.oversample_enabled == RENOISE.aa and not RENOISE.aa then
    smp.oversample_enabled = true
  end
end

local function learn(smp)                       -- an empty slot: Renoise's own
  if smp and not smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data then
    RENOISE.mode = smp.interpolation_mode
    RENOISE.aa = smp.oversample_enabled
  end
end

local function unwatch(list)
  for _, w in ipairs(list) do
    pcall(function() w[1]:remove_notifier(w[2]) end)
  end
end

local function watch_sample(list, smp)
  local st = { data = smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data, name = smp.name }
  local function on_buffer()
    local data = smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data
    if data and (not st.data or smp.name ~= st.name) then
      pcall(apply_new, smp)
      st.fresh = false
    elseif data then                 -- new audio, same name so far: a file
      st.fresh = true                -- loaded over it gets its name next
      W.fresh[#W.fresh + 1] = st
    end
    st.data, st.name = data, smp.name
  end
  local function on_name()
    if st.fresh then st.fresh = false pcall(apply_new, smp) end
    st.name = smp.name
  end
  smp.sample_buffer_observable:add_notifier(on_buffer)
  smp.name_observable:add_notifier(on_name)
  list[#list + 1] = { smp.sample_buffer_observable, on_buffer }
  list[#list + 1] = { smp.name_observable, on_name }
end

local function watch_instrument(inst)
  local w = { samples = {} }
  local function samples()
    unwatch(w.samples)
    w.samples = {}
    for _, smp in ipairs(inst.samples) do watch_sample(w.samples, smp) end
  end
  w.fn = function(ev)
    if ev.type == "insert" then learn(inst.samples[ev.index]) end
    samples()
  end
  inst.samples_observable:add_notifier(w.fn)
  w.obs = inst.samples_observable
  samples()
  return w
end

local function unwatch_all()
  for _, w in ipairs(W.insts) do
    unwatch(w.samples)
    pcall(function() w.obs:remove_notifier(w.fn) end)
  end
  W.insts = {}
end

local function watch_all()
  unwatch_all()
  local s = song()
  if not s then return end
  for _, inst in ipairs(s.instruments) do
    local ok, w = pcall(watch_instrument, inst)
    if ok then W.insts[#W.insts + 1] = w end
  end
end

local function on_instruments(ev)
  if ev.type == "insert" then
    local inst = song().instruments[ev.index]
    if inst then learn(inst.samples[1]) end
  end
  watch_all()
end

local function attach()
  local s = song()
  if not s then return end
  if W.song then
    pcall(function() W.song.instruments_observable:remove_notifier(on_instruments) end)
  end
  W.song = s
  s.instruments_observable:add_notifier(on_instruments)
  watch_all()
end

renoise.tool().app_new_document_observable:add_notifier(attach)
renoise.tool().app_release_document_observable:add_notifier(function()
  unwatch_all()
  if W.song then
    pcall(function() W.song.instruments_observable:remove_notifier(on_instruments) end)
  end
  W.song = nil
end)
-- a file loaded over a sample: its name follows within the same moment
renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:add_notifier(function()
  if #W.fresh > 0 then
    for _, st in ipairs(W.fresh) do st.fresh = false end
    W.fresh = {}
  end
end)
attach()

local function set_new(m)
  prefs.new_mode.value = m
  status("New samples: " .. (m == 0 and "Off (Renoise's default)" or MODES[m]))
end

local function toggle_new_aa()
  prefs.new_aa.value = not prefs.new_aa.value
  status("New samples: Anti-aliasing " .. (prefs.new_aa.value and "on"
         or "as Renoise sets it"))
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Menus and key bindings
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function entry(name, invoke, selected)
  renoise.tool():add_menu_entry { name = name, invoke = invoke,
                                  selected = selected }
end

-- one scope's entries under `base`: the four modes, then Anti-aliasing
local function scope_menu(base, scope)
  for i, m in ipairs(MODES) do
    entry(base .. scope .. ":" .. m,
          function() set_mode(scope, i) end,
          function() return common(scope) == i end)
  end
  entry("--- " .. base .. scope .. ":Anti-aliasing",
        function() toggle_aa(scope) end,
        function() return all_aa(scope) end)
end

-- Tools menu: everything
local TOOLS = "Main Menu:Tools:" .. TOOL .. ":"
entry(TOOLS .. "New Samples:Off (Renoise's Default)", function() set_new(0) end,
      function() return prefs.new_mode.value == 0 end)
for i, m in ipairs(MODES) do
  entry((i == 1 and "--- " or "") .. TOOLS .. "New Samples:" .. m,
        function() set_new(i) end,
        function() return prefs.new_mode.value == i end)
end
entry("--- " .. TOOLS .. "New Samples:Anti-aliasing On", toggle_new_aa,
      function() return prefs.new_aa.value end)
for _, scope in ipairs(SCOPES) do scope_menu(TOOLS, scope) end

-- right-click menus where the samples are
for _, place in ipairs { "Sample List", "Sample Editor" } do
  local base = place .. ":" .. TOOL .. ":"
  scope_menu(base, "Selected Sample")
  scope_menu(base, "Selected Instrument")
end
do
  local base = "Instrument Box:" .. TOOL .. ":"
  scope_menu(base, "Selected Instrument")
  scope_menu(base, "Whole Song")
end

-- key bindings
local function bind(name, fn)
  renoise.tool():add_keybinding {
    name = "Global:" .. TOOL .. ":" .. name,
    invoke = function(repeated) if not repeated then fn() end end,
  }
end
for _, scope in ipairs(SCOPES) do
  for i, m in ipairs(MODES) do
    bind(scope .. " - " .. m, function() set_mode(scope, i) end)
  end
  bind(scope .. " - Cycle", function() cycle(scope) end)
  bind(scope .. " - Toggle Anti-aliasing", function() toggle_aa(scope) end)
end
bind("New Samples - Cycle", function()
  set_new((prefs.new_mode.value + 1) % (#MODES + 1))
end)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Simple Interpolation
--
-- Set the interpolation (and Anti-aliasing) of samples from the Tools menu,
-- the sample list, sample editor and instrument box menus, or your own keys
-- (Preferences > Keys > Global > Simple Interpolation):
--
--   Selected Sample      the sample selected in Renoise
--   Selected Instrument  every sample of the selected instrument
--   Whole Song           every sample of every instrument
--   New Samples          a default for every sample you load, record or
--                        drag in from now on, in place of Renoise's own
--
-- by phaos & claude
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local TOOL = "Simple Interpolation"
local MODES = { "None", "Linear", "Cubic", "Sinc" }   -- = INTERPOLATE_*

local prefs = renoise.Document.create("SimpleInterpolationPreferences") {
  new_mode = 0,          -- New Samples: 0 Renoise's default, else 1 - 4
  new_aa = false,        -- New Samples: Anti-aliasing on
}
renoise.tool().preferences = prefs

local function status(msg)
  renoise.app():show_status(TOOL .. ": " .. msg)
end

local function song()
  local ok, s = pcall(renoise.song)
  return ok and s or nil
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Selected Sample / Selected Instrument / Whole Song
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local SCOPES = { "Selected Sample", "Selected Instrument", "Whole Song" }

-- the samples a scope means, and how to say so
local function targets(scope)
  local s, list = song(), {}
  if not s then return list, "" end
  if scope == "Selected Sample" then
    local smp = s.selected_sample
    if smp then list[1] = smp end
    return list, "Selected sample"
  end
  local insts = scope == "Selected Instrument" and { s.selected_instrument }
                or s.instruments
  for _, inst in ipairs(insts) do
    for _, smp in ipairs(inst.samples) do list[#list + 1] = smp end
  end
  local what = scope == "Selected Instrument" and "Selected instrument"
               or "Whole song"
  return list, string.format("%s (%d sample%s)", what, #list,
                             #list == 1 and "" or "s")
end

-- the interpolation all of them share (nil: none, or mixed)
local function common(scope)
  local list, m = targets(scope), nil
  for _, smp in ipairs(list) do
    if m and smp.interpolation_mode ~= m then return nil end
    m = smp.interpolation_mode
  end
  return m
end

local function all_aa(scope)
  local list = targets(scope)
  if #list == 0 then return false end
  for _, smp in ipairs(list) do
    if not smp.oversample_enabled then return false end
  end
  return true
end

-- change every sample of a scope: one undo step
local function change(scope, what_of, fn)
  local list, what = targets(scope)
  if #list == 0 then
    status(scope == "Selected Sample" and "No sample selected"
           or "No samples")
    return
  end
  pcall(function() song():describe_undo(TOOL .. ": " .. what_of) end)
  for _, smp in ipairs(list) do pcall(fn, smp) end
  status(what .. ": " .. what_of)
end

local function set_mode(scope, mode)
  change(scope, MODES[mode], function(smp) smp.interpolation_mode = mode end)
end

local function cycle(scope)
  local list = targets(scope)
  local m = common(scope) or (list[1] and list[1].interpolation_mode) or 3
  set_mode(scope, m % #MODES + 1)
end

local function toggle_aa(scope)
  local on = not all_aa(scope)
  change(scope, "Anti-aliasing " .. (on and "on" or "off"),
         function(smp) smp.oversample_enabled = on end)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- New Samples
--
-- A sample is new when audio arrives in an empty slot, or a file is loaded
-- over one (its audio and its name change together). It gets the default
-- only where it still has Renoise's own setting, so a sample that comes
-- with its own (a duplicate, an instrument file, another tool's choice) is
-- left alone. Renoise's own setting is read from the empty slots it makes.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local W = { song = nil, insts = {}, fresh = {} }
local RENOISE = { mode = 3, aa = false }       -- what an empty slot has

local function apply_new(smp)
  local m, aa = prefs.new_mode.value, prefs.new_aa.value
  if m > 0 and smp.interpolation_mode == RENOISE.mode and m ~= RENOISE.mode then
    smp.interpolation_mode = m
  end
  if aa and smp.oversample_enabled == RENOISE.aa and not RENOISE.aa then
    smp.oversample_enabled = true
  end
end

local function learn(smp)                       -- an empty slot: Renoise's own
  if smp and not smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data then
    RENOISE.mode = smp.interpolation_mode
    RENOISE.aa = smp.oversample_enabled
  end
end

local function unwatch(list)
  for _, w in ipairs(list) do
    pcall(function() w[1]:remove_notifier(w[2]) end)
  end
end

local function watch_sample(list, smp)
  local st = { data = smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data, name = smp.name }
  local function on_buffer()
    local data = smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data
    if data and (not st.data or smp.name ~= st.name) then
      pcall(apply_new, smp)
      st.fresh = false
    elseif data then                 -- new audio, same name so far: a file
      st.fresh = true                -- loaded over it gets its name next
      W.fresh[#W.fresh + 1] = st
    end
    st.data, st.name = data, smp.name
  end
  local function on_name()
    if st.fresh then st.fresh = false pcall(apply_new, smp) end
    st.name = smp.name
  end
  smp.sample_buffer_observable:add_notifier(on_buffer)
  smp.name_observable:add_notifier(on_name)
  list[#list + 1] = { smp.sample_buffer_observable, on_buffer }
  list[#list + 1] = { smp.name_observable, on_name }
end

local function watch_instrument(inst)
  local w = { samples = {} }
  local function samples()
    unwatch(w.samples)
    w.samples = {}
    for _, smp in ipairs(inst.samples) do watch_sample(w.samples, smp) end
  end
  w.fn = function(ev)
    if ev.type == "insert" then learn(inst.samples[ev.index]) end
    samples()
  end
  inst.samples_observable:add_notifier(w.fn)
  w.obs = inst.samples_observable
  samples()
  return w
end

local function unwatch_all()
  for _, w in ipairs(W.insts) do
    unwatch(w.samples)
    pcall(function() w.obs:remove_notifier(w.fn) end)
  end
  W.insts = {}
end

local function watch_all()
  unwatch_all()
  local s = song()
  if not s then return end
  for _, inst in ipairs(s.instruments) do
    local ok, w = pcall(watch_instrument, inst)
    if ok then W.insts[#W.insts + 1] = w end
  end
end

local function on_instruments(ev)
  if ev.type == "insert" then
    local inst = song().instruments[ev.index]
    if inst then learn(inst.samples[1]) end
  end
  watch_all()
end

local function attach()
  local s = song()
  if not s then return end
  if W.song then
    pcall(function() W.song.instruments_observable:remove_notifier(on_instruments) end)
  end
  W.song = s
  s.instruments_observable:add_notifier(on_instruments)
  watch_all()
end

renoise.tool().app_new_document_observable:add_notifier(attach)
renoise.tool().app_release_document_observable:add_notifier(function()
  unwatch_all()
  if W.song then
    pcall(function() W.song.instruments_observable:remove_notifier(on_instruments) end)
  end
  W.song = nil
end)
-- a file loaded over a sample: its name follows within the same moment
renoise.tool().app_idle_observable:add_notifier(function()
  if #W.fresh > 0 then
    for _, st in ipairs(W.fresh) do st.fresh = false end
    W.fresh = {}
  end
end)
attach()

local function set_new(m)
  prefs.new_mode.value = m
  status("New samples: " .. (m == 0 and "Off (Renoise's default)" or MODES[m]))
end

local function toggle_new_aa()
  prefs.new_aa.value = not prefs.new_aa.value
  status("New samples: Anti-aliasing " .. (prefs.new_aa.value and "on"
         or "as Renoise sets it"))
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Menus and key bindings
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function entry(name, invoke, selected)
  renoise.tool():add_menu_entry { name = name, invoke = invoke,
                                  selected = selected }
end

-- one scope's entries under `base`: the four modes, then Anti-aliasing
local function scope_menu(base, scope)
  for i, m in ipairs(MODES) do
    entry(base .. scope .. ":" .. m,
          function() set_mode(scope, i) end,
          function() return common(scope) == i end)
  end
  entry("--- " .. base .. scope .. ":Anti-aliasing",
        function() toggle_aa(scope) end,
        function() return all_aa(scope) end)
end

-- Tools menu: everything
local TOOLS = "Main Menu:Tools:" .. TOOL .. ":"
entry(TOOLS .. "New Samples:Off (Renoise's Default)", function() set_new(0) end,
      function() return prefs.new_mode.value == 0 end)
for i, m in ipairs(MODES) do
  entry((i == 1 and "--- " or "") .. TOOLS .. "New Samples:" .. m,
        function() set_new(i) end,
        function() return prefs.new_mode.value == i end)
end
entry("--- " .. TOOLS .. "New Samples:Anti-aliasing On", toggle_new_aa,
      function() return prefs.new_aa.value end)
for _, scope in ipairs(SCOPES) do scope_menu(TOOLS, scope) end

-- right-click menus where the samples are
for _, place in ipairs { "Sample List", "Sample Editor" } do
  local base = place .. ":" .. TOOL .. ":"
  scope_menu(base, "Selected Sample")
  scope_menu(base, "Selected Instrument")
end
do
  local base = "Instrument Box:" .. TOOL .. ":"
  scope_menu(base, "Selected Instrument")
  scope_menu(base, "Whole Song")
end

-- key bindings
local function bind(name, fn)
  renoise.tool():add_keybinding {
    name = "Global:" .. TOOL .. ":" .. name,
    invoke = function(repeated) if not repeated then fn() end end,
  }
end
for _, scope in ipairs(SCOPES) do
  for i, m in ipairs(MODES) do
    bind(scope .. " - " .. m, function() set_mode(scope, i) end)
  end
  bind(scope .. " - Cycle", function() cycle(scope) end)
  bind(scope .. " - Toggle Anti-aliasing", function() toggle_aa(scope) end)
end
bind("New Samples - Cycle", function()
  set_new((prefs.new_mode.value + 1) % (#MODES + 1))
end)

function PakettiGlobalSample(interpolation)
  local song=renoise.song()
  local interpolation_modes={"none","linear","cubic","sinc"}
  
  local interpolation_name=interpolation_modes[interpolation] or "unknown"

  for i=1,#song.instruments do
    local instrument=song.instruments[i]
    
    if instrument==nil then
      renoise.app():show_status("Instrument "..i.." is nil, skipping.")
    elseif #instrument.samples==0 then
      renoise.app():show_status("Instrument "..i.." has no samples, skipping.")
    else
      for y=1,#instrument.samples do
        instrument.samples[y].interpolation_mode=interpolation
      end
      renoise.app():show_status("Set interpolation for all samples in instrument "..i..".")
    end
  end
  
  renoise.app():show_status("Finished setting interpolation to "..interpolation_name.." for all instruments.")
end

function on_sample_count_change()
    if not preferences._0G01_Loader.value then return end
    local song=renoise.song()
    if not song or #song.tracks == 0 or song.selected_track.type ~= renoise.Track.TRACK_TYPE_SEQUENCER then return end

    local selected_track_index = song.selected_track_index
    local new_track_idx = selected_track_index + 1

    song:insert_track_at(new_track_idx)
    local line = song.patterns[song.selected_pattern_index].tracks[new_track_idx]:line(1)
    song.selected_track_index = new_track_idx
    line.note_columns[1].note_string = "C-4"
    line.note_columns[1].instrument_value = song.selected_instrument_index - 1
    line.effect_columns[1].number_string = "0G"
    line.effect_columns[1].amount_value = 01
end

function manage_sample_count_observer(attach)
    local song=renoise.song()
    local instr = song.selected_instrument
    if attach then
        if not instr.samples_observable:has_notifier(on_sample_count_change) then
            instr.samples_observable:add_notifier(on_sample_count_change)
        end
    else
        if instr.samples_observable:has_notifier(on_sample_count_change) then
            instr.samples_observable:remove_notifier(on_sample_count_change)
        end
    end
end

function PakettiGlobalSample(interpolation)
  local song=renoise.song()
  local interpolation_modes={"none","linear","cubic","sinc"}
  
  local interpolation_name=interpolation_modes[interpolation] or "unknown"

  for i=1,#song.instruments do
    local instrument=song.instruments[i]
    
    if instrument==nil then
      renoise.app():show_status("Instrument "..i.." is nil, skipping.")
    elseif #instrument.samples==0 then
      renoise.app():show_status("Instrument "..i.." has no samples, skipping.")
    else
      for y=1,#instrument.samples do
        instrument.samples[y].interpolation_mode=interpolation
      end
      renoise.app():show_status("Set interpolation for all samples in instrument "..i..".")
    end
  end
  
  renoise.app():show_status("Finished setting interpolation to "..interpolation_name.." for all instruments.")
end

## What it actually controls

This tool controls sample playback interpolation (`sample.interpolation_mode`: None, Linear, Cubic, Sinc) and anti-aliasing (`sample.oversample_enabled`). It does not interpolate pattern values, notes, automation, or audio destructively. Its “Anti-aliasing” is the same property Paketti calls Oversampling.

Three scopes are available: selected sample, all samples of selected instrument, and all samples of every instrument in the song. Each has four explicit interpolation setters, a cycle keybinding, and an anti-aliasing toggle. Cycling uses the shared mode if uniform, otherwise the first target sample's mode, then advances and sets every target to that mode. Anti-aliasing turns off only when all targets are already on; otherwise it turns all on.

The Tools menu offers all scopes plus New Samples preferences. Sample List and Sample Editor menus offer selected sample/instrument; Instrument Box offers selected instrument/whole song. Mode checkmarks appear only for a uniform mode; anti-aliasing is checked only if every target is enabled. All callbacks return booleans. Keybindings suppress repeats. It supplies undo descriptions; there are no MIDI mappings in this tool.

## Existing Paketti coverage

| Capability | Paketti source | Comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Set selected sample to any of four modes | PakettiTkna.lua:368 selectedSampleInterpolation; keybindings at :430 | Already covered |
| Set selected instrument samples to any of four modes | PakettiRequests.lua:2031 setSelectedInstrumentInterpolation; keybindings at :2038 | Already covered |
| Set every sample in every instrument to any of four modes | PakettiRequests.lua:9039 PakettiGlobalSample; keybindings at :9064 | Already covered; the user remembered correctly |
| Selected sample oversampling on/off/toggle | PakettiTkna.lua:376, :384, :392 | Already covered; explicit on/off is more than SimpleInterpolation offers |
| Whole-song oversampling on/off | PakettiRequests.lua:9069 PakettiGlobalOversample; keybindings at :9091 | Already covered, but lacks the tool's collective toggle |
| Defaults in Paketti loading/generation paths | Paketti0G01_Loader.lua:357 pakettiLoaderInterpolation, :359 pakettiLoaderOverSampling, UI at :2203–2215; consumers throughout sample loaders, recorder and generators | Existing preferences, but scoped to paths that apply them |

| Pattern/automation/phrase interpolation | PakettiRequests.lua, PakettiInterpolateBeyond.lua, PakettiAutomationInterpolate.lua, PakettiPhraseEditor.lua | Separate features; this tool contributes nothing to them |

Searches for the existing setter symbols found their registrations as keybindings, rather than the checked sample-context menu family supplied here. Searches did not find equivalent interpolation cycle commands or a dedicated selected-instrument oversampling setter/toggle.

## What is missing relative to this tool

1. A consistent checked menu family across Tools, Sample List, Sample Editor and Instrument Box, showing uniform versus mixed modes and the all-enabled oversampling state.
2. Interpolation cycling for selected sample, selected instrument and whole song, with defined mixed-mode behavior.
3. Selected-instrument oversampling control and collective instrument/song toggles. Paketti already has song-wide explicit on/off and sample on/off/toggle.
4. An optional default watcher for new audio arriving through native Renoise operations, rather than only code paths that apply Paketti loader preferences.
5. Consistent undo descriptions, no-target feedback and repeat suppression around these sample-setting commands. The inspected Paketti setters do not explicitly describe undo steps or suppress repeated key invocations; actual Renoise undo grouping was not tested.

## New Samples: useful idea, imperfect detector

Its independent persistent preferences are interpolation Off/None/Linear/Cubic/Sinc and Anti-aliasing On (disabled means leave Renoise's setting). Turning either default off does not change existing samples.

It subscribes to instrument-list changes, sample-list changes, sample-buffer replacement and sample-name changes. This aims to preserve settings in duplicates and instrument imports, but provenance cannot be inferred from equality: an explicitly Cubic incoming sample can be indistinguishable from an untouched default and get overridden. Conversely, already-populated samples newly inserted into an instrument are initially watched as existing data; registration alone does not apply defaults to them. Same-name replacements can evade the name-change heuristic. These are code-level limitations, not runtime-confirmed failures.

Per-sample writes are wrapped in pcall and failure results are ignored, including manual bulk changes, so success statuses do not prove every target accepted a change. Empty-slot baseline learning is also heuristic: it does not verify an empty slot is untouched by another tool/user.

Add the coherent menu/checkmark layer, three cycle commands, instrument oversampling controls and collective toggles. -- Helper function to conditionally add menu entry (QUEUED, not immediate)
-- Usage: PakettiAddMenuEntry{name="...", invoke=function() end}
function PakettiAddMenuEntry(args)
  if not PakettiShouldRegisterMenuEntry(args.name) then
    return false
  end
  table.insert(PakettiPendingMenuEntries, args)
  return true
end

-- DRY helper for a checkbox/toggle menu entry bound to a boolean preference, anywhere
-- in the menu tree. The codebase repeated this exact shape dozens of times: flip
-- preferences.X.value, preferences:save_as("preferences.xml"), show an "ON"/"OFF"
-- status, and a `selected` callback returning the same value so the menu draws a
-- checkmark. This wraps all of it. It routes through PakettiAddMenuEntry, so it honors
-- the master menu toggle, the per-context Menu Configuration preference, alphabetical
-- sorting, and the duplicate guard exactly like every other Paketti menu entry.
--
-- You pass the FULL menu `name` and the preference node to toggle. A leading "--"
-- separator on the name is preserved. Three ways to use it:
--
-- Pure preference toggle — helper generates flip + save + status + checkmark:
--   PakettiAddMenuToggleEntry{name="Main Menu:Options:Follow Page Pattern Toggle", pref=preferences.pakettiFollowPagePattern}
-- Custom invoke (a named toggle fn that does extra work) but checkmark from the pref:
--   PakettiAddMenuToggleEntry{name="...", invoke=PakettiToggleFollowPagePattern, pref=preferences.pakettiFollowPagePattern}
-- State the checkmark reads from a getter (a runtime global or a state function) rather
-- than a preference — the DRY form for toggles whose state is NOT a pakettiPreferences
-- boolean. You still supply `invoke`; the helper just wraps `get` as a strict boolean:
--   PakettiAddMenuToggleEntry{name="...", invoke=PakettiFrameCalculatorToggle, get=PakettiFrameCalculatorIsEnabled}
--   PakettiAddMenuToggleEntry{name="...", invoke=function() ... end, get=function() return SomeGlobal end}
-- Escape hatch — your own invoke AND selected (helper only adds nothing but routing):
--   PakettiAddMenuToggleEntry{name="...", invoke=function() ... end, selected=function() return ... end}
-- Extras: status="..." overrides the status prefix (default: the leaf minus a trailing
-- " Toggle"); after=function(on) ... end runs right after the flip (e.g. apply live).
function PakettiAddMenuToggleEntry(args)
  local raw = args.name or ""
  local dashes = raw:match("^%-*") or ""
  local path = raw:sub(#dashes + 1)
  local full_name = dashes .. path

  -- The visible leaf (last path segment, trailing " Toggle" stripped) is the default
  -- status prefix, e.g. "...:Sononymph Autostart Toggle" -> "Sononymph Autostart".
  local leaf = path:match("([^:]+)$") or path
  local status_label = args.status or (leaf:gsub("%s+Toggle$", ""))

-- FEATURE-CARD >> features/sample-playback-quality.feature
-- Phaos's SimpleInterpolation inspired these checked, scoped quality controls.
do
  local modes = {"None", "Linear", "Cubic", "Sinc"}
  local scopes = {"Selected Sample", "Selected Instrument", "Whole Song"}
  local function PakettiSampleQualityTargets(scope)
    local ok, song = pcall(renoise.song)
    if not ok or not song then return {} end
    if scope == "Selected Sample" then
      return song.selected_sample and {song.selected_sample} or {}
    end
    local result = {}
    local instruments = scope == "Selected Instrument" and {song.selected_instrument} or song.instruments
    for _, instrument in ipairs(instruments) do
      for _, sample in ipairs(instrument.samples) do result[#result + 1] = sample end
    end
    return result
  end
  local function all_match(scope, field, value)
    local samples = PakettiSampleQualityTargets(scope)
    if #samples == 0 then return false end
    for _, sample in ipairs(samples) do
      if sample[field] ~= value then return false end
    end
    return true
  end
  local function PakettiSampleQualityChange(scope, mode, oversampling)
    local samples = PakettiSampleQualityTargets(scope)
    if #samples == 0 then
      renoise.app():show_status("Paketti: No samples in " .. scope)
      return
    end
    if mode == "cycle" then mode = samples[1].interpolation_mode % 4 + 1 end
    if oversampling == "toggle" then oversampling = not all_match(scope, "oversample_enabled", true) end
    renoise.song():describe_undo("Sample Playback Quality: " .. scope)
    if mode then
      if scope == "Selected Sample" then selectedSampleInterpolation(mode)
      elseif scope == "Selected Instrument" then setSelectedInstrumentInterpolation(mode)
      else PakettiGlobalSample(mode) end
    elseif scope == "Selected Sample" then
      if oversampling then selectedSampleOversampleOn() else selectedSampleOversampleOff() end
    elseif scope == "Whole Song" then
      PakettiGlobalOversample(oversampling)
    else
      for _, sample in ipairs(samples) do sample.oversample_enabled = oversampling end
    end
    local setting = mode and modes[mode] or ("Oversampling " .. (oversampling and "On" or "Off"))
    renoise.app():show_status("Paketti: " .. scope .. " — " .. setting .. " (" .. #samples .. " samples)")
  end
  local function add_scope(base, scope)
    for index, label in ipairs(modes) do
      local mode = index
      PakettiAddMenuEntry{name=base .. scope .. ":" .. label,
        invoke=function() PakettiSampleQualityChange(scope, mode) end,
        selected=function() return all_match(scope, "interpolation_mode", mode) end}
    end
    PakettiAddMenuEntry{name=base .. scope .. ":Cycle Interpolation",
      invoke=function() PakettiSampleQualityChange(scope, "cycle") end}
    PakettiAddMenuEntry{name=base .. scope .. ":Oversampling",
      invoke=function() PakettiSampleQualityChange(scope, nil, "toggle") end,
      selected=function() return all_match(scope, "oversample_enabled", true) end}
  end
  for _, scope in ipairs(scopes) do
    add_scope("Main Menu:Tools:Paketti:Sample Playback Quality:", scope)
    for _, action in ipairs({"Cycle Interpolation", "Toggle Oversampling"}) do
      local cycle = action == "Cycle Interpolation"
      local function invoke()
        if cycle then PakettiSampleQualityChange(scope, "cycle")
        else PakettiSampleQualityChange(scope, nil, "toggle") end
      end
      local name = action .. " in " .. scope
      -- Selected-sample oversampling already has an existing toggle keybinding.
      if cycle or scope ~= "Selected Sample" then
        renoise.tool():add_keybinding{name="Global:Paketti:" .. name,
          invoke=function(repeated) if not repeated then invoke() end end}
      end
      renoise.tool():add_midi_mapping{name="Paketti:" .. name,
        invoke=function(message) if message:is_trigger() then invoke() end end}
    end
  end
  for _, context in ipairs({"Sample List", "Sample Editor"}) do
    add_scope(context .. ":Paketti:Sample Playback Quality:", "Selected Sample")
    add_scope(context .. ":Paketti:Sample Playback Quality:", "Selected Instrument")
  end
  add_scope("Instrument Box:Paketti:Sample Playback Quality:", "Selected Instrument")
  add_scope("Instrument Box:Paketti:Sample Playback Quality:", "Whole Song")
end
